SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Heritage Global Valuations (“HGV”), a division of Heritage Global Inc. (NASDAQ: HGBL), a leading appraisal and liquidation firm, today announced that Michael Kara has joined the firm as Senior Vice President of Inventory Appraisals.

Kara brings extensive experience conducting inventory appraisals for asset-based lenders, financial institutions and private equity firms. His work includes valuations of e-commerce, retail, wholesale and industrial inventories, as well as collateral analysis and asset recovery assessments supporting financing transactions.

Prior to joining HGV, Kara served as President of Jay, Cobb & Marley, where he held several positions during his tenure. His earlier experience includes roles with SB Capital Group, GoIndustry-DoveBid and The Daley-Hodkin Group. Throughout his career, he has completed appraisal assignments across a range of industries, including consumer products, pharmaceuticals, electronics, building materials and manufacturing.

“Michael understands the importance of delivering practical, well-supported valuations, particularly as e-commerce continues to shape the inventory appraisal landscape,” said Mike Goldstein, Executive Managing Director of Heritage Global Valuations. “His approach to client service aligns well with ours, and we're pleased to have him join the team.”

“I'm excited to join Heritage Global Valuations and work alongside its experienced appraisal team,” said Kara. “I look forward to collaborating with my colleagues and building relationships with clients while contributing to the high level of service HGV provides.”

For inquiries regarding inventory appraisal services, contact Michael Kara at mkara@hginc.com.

Heritage Global Valuations (“HGV") is a division of Heritage Global Inc. (NASDAQ: HGBL). HGV operates under the Industrial Assets business unit and specializes in the valuation of commercial & industrial assets including inventories and machinery & equipment (“M&E”). Valuations are developed based on a number of factors, including an extensive proprietary database containing information about past transactions, firsthand knowledge of the market, extensive analyses, and relationships with original equipment manufacturers (“OEMs”) and dealers of industrial assets. Taking into account the economic and competitive environment of the industry in which the business operates, assuring an accurate and reliable appraisal which enables clients to make timely strategic decisions.

Heritage Global Inc. (“HG”) values and monetizes industrial & financial assets by providing acquisition, disposition, valuation, and lending services for surplus and distressed assets. This aids in facilitating the circular economy by diverting useful industrial assets from landfills and operating an ethical supply chain by overseeing post-sale account activity of financial assets. Specialties consist of acting as an adviser, in addition to acquiring or brokering turnkey manufacturing facilities, surplus industrial machinery and equipment, industrial inventories, real estate, and charged-off account receivable portfolios through its two business units: Industrial Assets and Financial Assets.

CONROE, TX / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / Olenox Industries Inc. (NASDAQ:OLOX) ("Olenox" or the "Company"), an integrated energy and infrastructure company, today announced that the Railroad Commission of Texas has issued Olenox Corp. Permit No. 10822, a Permit to Operate a Pipeline in Texas, authorizing operation of the Company's central Texas natural-gas pipeline system.

The permit follows a regulatory process that extended for more than one year and represents a major operating milestone for Olenox. With the permit now issued, the Company can move forward with the staged activation, restoration and expansion of the pipeline system while pursuing new natural-gas supply and power-generation opportunities.

The permit covers 95.19 miles of pipeline across Brown, Coleman and McCulloch counties and classifies the system as a gas utility. Olenox Corp. is identified as the pipeline owner, operator and economic operator. The permit was issued October 30, 2026 and is valid through May 31, 2028.

Olenox is currently working to secure an initial natural-gas capacity of approximately 1 million cubic feet per day ("MMcf/d") for the system. The Company plans to use that initial capacity to support the staged deployment of a 4-megawatt ("MW") containerized power-generation site, with initial power production targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

"Receiving this permit is a significant step forward for Olenox and the result of more than a year of regulatory and operational work," said Mike McLaren, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Olenox. "We can now begin moving this pipeline from an existing infrastructure asset into an operating platform for natural-gas transportation and distributed power generation. Our initial objective is to line up approximately 1 MMcf per day of gas capacity, deploy the first 4 MW site and build from there as pipeline throughput and market opportunities increase."

The initial 4 MW site is expected to serve as the first deployment under Olenox's broader strategy to develop multiple containerized power projects of 10 MW or less across the United States and Canada. The distributed model is designed to place scalable generating capacity near available energy resources and expand individual sites in stages as gas supply, infrastructure and customer demand support additional capacity.

Olenox intends to evaluate additional gas-supply arrangements, pipeline restoration requirements, compression and facility upgrades, and future off-take and power-generation opportunities across the system. As throughput increases, the Company expects to assess additional containerized generation deployments that could extend the economic value of the pipeline and its surrounding energy infrastructure.

The planned 1 MMcf/d capacity, 4 MW deployment, Q1 2027 production timeline and future project expansion are targets and have not yet been achieved. Development remains subject to securing gas supply, generation equipment, financing, site readiness, engineering, construction, interconnection, applicable permits and approvals, and other customary operating requirements.

About Olenox Industries Inc.

Olenox Industries Inc. (NASDAQ:OLOX) is an integrated energy and infrastructure company focused on acquiring, developing and operating assets across the oil and natural gas, energy services, power generation, modular infrastructure and digital-compute sectors. Through its subsidiaries, Olenox is building a vertically integrated platform designed to connect energy resources with power-intensive infrastructure while delivering engineered and modular solutions across industrial markets.

Celebrates 160 years of customer service, implements vision for the future


SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- San Jose Water (“SJW” or “the Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of H2O America (NASDAQ: HTO), today unveiled H2O Next, one part of the company’s long-term vision to develop alternative water supply sources that provide affordable and sustainable local water supply to customers for generations to come, and shared the first look at the mobile water purification lab pilot facility and interactive experience. SJW, celebrating 160 years of service this month, expects the H2O Next lab to begin accepting visitors at its McLaughlin pumping station base location in fall 2027, ahead of the two-year timeline announced in April.

“When San Jose Water was founded in 1866, a promise to deliver good and pure water meant two tanks and about 400 neighbors,” said Tanya Moniz-Witten, president of San Jose Water. “Every generation since then has looked ahead to what this community would need next, and San Jose Water has been here to meet challenges in prudent, innovative ways for our customers. H2O Next is part of how we’ll continue doing that, and we look forward to this pilot demonstration and learning lab being accessible to customers and community members to see it up close, ask tough questions and help shape what comes next.”

About half of the water SJW delivers today is imported from outside of Silicon Valley, and H2O Next will demonstrate the technology SJW could use at scale to make purified recycled water an alternative local supply that holds up in drought conditions and meets customers’ expectations.

Lab visitors will be able to follow recycled water through each stage of the water purification process and see how the technology purifies it to meet strict federal and state drinking water standards. SJW experts will be available to answer questions. Community groups, schools and event organizers can request a visit to the lab. A new video featuring President Tanya Moniz-Witten and Jake Walsh, vice president of engineering, with a 3D tour of the planned mobile lab, is available at sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext.

Also on the innovation front, SJW is completing installation of its smart meters, finishing a three-year systemwide rollout by the end of 2026. The meters record water use every hour so customers can monitor their water usage and spot potential leaks early. SJW sent more than 44,000 leak notifications in 2025 and more than 100,000 through July 2026, giving customers practical, timely information they can use to reduce water loss and better manage household costs. Combined with acoustic leak detection on about 14,000 of the company’s 20,000 fire hydrants, the technology helps SJW find and fix problems before they become costly main breaks. Together, these technologies have helped SJW keep its water loss rate to about 8%, compared with a national average of roughly 14%.

Those tools build on steady investment in the water system behind every tap. Since 2021, SJW has invested more than $1 billion to upgrade infrastructure and replace pipes, tanks and well pumps. At its Cambrian Station, which serves about 225,000 people from Japantown to the Rose Garden, SJW brought the first of two new 8-million-gallon, seismically resilient tanks online in February, replacing earthen reservoirs that had served the community for more than a century. The company also performs more than 18,000 water quality tests each year across dozens of locations to confirm its teams and facilities meet water quality standards, and its security teams block roughly 5 million attempted cyberattacks every day to protect the systems that have kept water flowing for 160 years and will continue to serve Silicon Valley for generations to come.

To watch the H2O Next video and 3D tour, visit sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext. SJW’s 160th anniversary video is available at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r3eF_ajkXDw. Photos, video and background materials for media are available for download at sjwater.com/SJWH2ONext.

About San Jose Water

Founded in 1866, San Jose Water is a regulated private utility and one of the largest and most technically sophisticated urban water systems in the United States. The company serves more than one million people in the greater San Jose metropolitan area. San Jose Water is owned by H2O America, a publicly traded company listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the symbol HTO. H2O America also owns Connecticut Water Company in Connecticut, Maine Water Company in Maine and Texas Water Company in Texas. To learn more about San Jose Water, visit www.sjwater.com.

BOSTON, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Capstone Partners, a leading middle market investment banking firm, is pleased to announce the appointments of Ji Sang Lee as Managing Director and Head of Buy-Side Advisory and Michael Mathews as Managing Director and Head of Technology & Digital Advisory within its Financial Advisory Services (FAS) Group. The firm has also added Managing Directors Tim Ludwick to its Sponsor Coverage Group and Chris Fieschko to its Technology, Media & Telecom ("TMT") Industry Group.

The appointments reflect Capstone's continued investment in senior talent. The two new practice leaders expand the firm's advisory capabilities, while the additional Managing Directors extend its reach across private equity sponsors and sector-focused investment banking. Together, the hires position Capstone to serve middle market clients with greater depth and align with its broader growth initiatives.

Lee brings diverse experience to his role as Head of Buy-Side Advisory, spanning transaction origination and execution, business development, and leadership and strategic growth. He will lead the firm's buy-side engagements with private equity firms and corporate clients, supporting inorganic growth initiatives through proprietary acquisitions and buy-and-build strategies.

As the FAS Group's Head of Technology & Digital Advisory, Mathews adds operational and transformation depth supported by his 30-year career driving growth and value creation for clients. His background in technology transformation, M&A integration, AI and automation, and performance improvement deepens the FAS Group's advisory service offerings in key areas of opportunity.

Supporting this momentum, Ludwick joined the firm's Sponsor Coverage Group earlier this fall, leading coverage of middle market private equity firms and their key decision makers. He has more than 15 years of investment banking experience, with a career-long focus on supporting financial sponsors.

Capstone also deepens its industry investment banking coverage with the addition of Fieschko to its TMT Group. With a focus on the Healthcare IT sector, he brings strong investment banking and financial advisory experience at the intersection of key subsegments in Healthcare, Technology, and Services.

"The addition of Ji, Michael, Tim, and Chris reflects our focus on thoughtfully expanding the capabilities we bring to clients," said Jarrad Zalkin, Head of Investment Banking at Capstone Partners. "Together, they bring significant experience and relationships that reinforce the collaborative, sector-focused approach behind our growth in the middle market." 

The appointments underscore the momentum continuing to build across the firm. Closing out a year of significant growth that has brought Capstone to over 300 professionals, the firm continues to add senior leaders who deepen its sector knowledge and broaden its advisory capabilities for business owners, private equity firms, and corporate clients. As Capstone grows, it remains focused on delivering integrated, sector-specific advice to clients at every stage of the business lifecycle.

ABOUT CAPSTONE PARTNERS

For over 20 years, the firm has been a trusted advisor to leading middle market companies, offering a fully integrated range of investment banking and financial advisory services uniquely tailored to help owners, investors, and creditors through each stage of the company's lifecycle. Capstone's services include M&A advisory, debt and equity placement, corporate restructuring, special situations, valuation and fairness opinions and financial advisory services. Headquartered in Boston, the firm has 300+ professionals in multiple offices across the U.S. With 12 dedicated industry groups, Capstone delivers sector-specific expertise through large, cross-functional teams. Earn more on every business trip and with every purchase

SINGAPORE, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Trident Digital Tech Holdings Ltd (Nasdaq: TDTH) (“Trident” or the “Company”), a Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure and technology holding company, today announced that it has entered into a memorandum of understanding (the “MOU”) with Guang Yao Development (M) Sdn. Bhd. (“Guang Yao”), a Malaysian company positioned to provide hydrogen power and battery energy storage solutions for data centres, for the proposed acquisition of 51% of the issued share capital of Guang Yao (the “Proposed Acquisition”).

The MOU, signed today, sets an indicative equity value of US$30 million for 100% of Guang Yao and an indicative consideration of US$15.3 million for the 51% interest, payable in cash at completion. Upon completion, Guang Yao would become a subsidiary of Trident, and Trident would be entitled to appoint a majority of Guang Yao’s board of directors.

Key Terms of the MOU

  • Stake: 51% of the issued share capital of Guang Yao on a fully diluted basis, to be acquired from Guang Yao’s shareholders.
  • Valuation and consideration: indicative equity value of US$30 million on a 100% basis; indicative consideration of US$15.3 million in cash, subject to adjustment following due diligence and an independent valuation.
  • Exclusivity: Guang Yao has agreed to deal exclusively with Trident in respect of any sale of its shares while the MOU is in effect.
  • Timetable: due diligence and independent valuation through December 11, 2026, with a target date of December 18, 2026 for the signing of definitive agreements and completion, and a long-stop date of January 31, 2027.
  • Governance: following completion, Trident and Guang Yao’s remaining shareholders would enter into a shareholders’ agreement on customary terms for a controlling shareholder.

Completion is subject to, among other things, the execution of definitive agreements, satisfactory due diligence, an independent valuation supporting the consideration, board approvals of both companies, compliance with the Nasdaq Listing Rules and U.S. securities laws, and the receipt of required regulatory and third-party approvals in Malaysia.

Powering the Infrastructure Behind Digital Growth

Data centres need power that is reliable and, increasingly, lower in carbon. The Proposed Acquisition would give Trident a presence in hydrogen power, which forms the core of Guang Yao’s business, and in battery energy storage, extending the Company’s digital infrastructure strategy into the energy layer that supports it.

“Every data centre runs on power, and the demand for power that is dependable and clean is only growing,” said Soon Huat Lim, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Trident. “A controlling stake in Guang Yao would take Trident from building digital infrastructure to also supplying the energy behind it. We look forward to completing our due diligence and working with Guang Yao and its shareholders towards definitive agreements.”

The Proposed Acquisition complements Trident’s existing operating platforms, which include TDTHAI, the Company’s enterprise artificial intelligence business; the IRMA Engine Asia joint venture with Digital Innovations Group; and Trident Aliska Digital Tech Ghana Ltd., which operates the Sikaflow platform and supports the Ghana Revenue Authority digital tax platform.

Guang Yao Development (M) Sdn. Bhd. (Registration No. 201101035846 (963980-A)) is a private company incorporated in Malaysia. Guang Yao is positioned to provide hydrogen power solutions and, to a lesser extent, battery energy storage solutions for data centres.

STOCKHOLM, November 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioArctic AB's (publ) (Nasdaq Stockholm: BIOA B) partner Eisai today presented new results from the real-world Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease (LEADER) study[1]. The data showed that patients treated with Leqembi had a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease dementia compared with a matched natural history cohort through 36 months of treatment. The new analysis included 560 patients treated with Leqembi across 13 clinical sites in the US.

The data were presented at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference in Boston and represent the largest analysis of the ongoing LEADER study reported to date. The results provide further insights into treatment with Leqembi in clinical practice, including disease progression, amyloid clearance, treatment persistence, expanded subcutaneous maintenance treatment experience and safety. The findings were presented alongside an international real-world meta-analysis of approximately 5,000 patients treated with Leqembi.

LEADER study key findings

LEADER patients showed slower progression compared to ADNI control[2]:

  • In a pre-specified comparison of patients in LEADER (N=504) with an ADNI-weighted external control cohort (N=573), patients treated with Leqembi had a 76% lower rate of progression to moderate or severe Alzheimer's disease dementia through 36 months (HR 0.24; 95% CI, 0.15–0.39).

More than 8 in 10 patients remained stable or improved[3]:

  • Among 546 patients whose change in disease stage could be assessed after an average of approximately 18 months of treatment, 81.1% were reported as stable or improved compared with baseline. Of these patients, 75.8% remained stable and 5.3% improved.
  • Results were generally consistent across groups defined by sex, race, ethnicity, APOE genotype and concomitant antithrombotic use.
  • At the time of chart extraction, 87.5% of the 560 patients remained on Leqembi treatment, with an average treatment duration of approximately 19 months.

Most patients estimated to remain in early Alzheimer's disease:

  • Among all 560 patients in the study, 95.0% were estimated to remain in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease through three years of treatment, based on statistical modeling of observed real-world patient data.

New real-world evidence shows amyloid clearance:

  • Among 43 patients across six sites performing both baseline and follow-up amyloid PET scans, 77% (33) became amyloid-negative at a median follow-up of 18.1 months. (IQR 16.4–18.7 months).

Expanding experience with Leqembi maintenance therapy:

  • Of the patients who reached 18 months of treatment, 91.7% remained on Leqembi. A total of 218 patients transitioned to intravenous (IV) maintenance treatment once-every-four-weeks., Following approval of once-weekly subcutaneous (SC) maintenance treatment, 64 patients transitioned to that regimen.
  • Among patients receiving monthly IV maintenance treatment, 71.1% remained stable after an average of 26 months from treatment initiation. Among patients receiving weekly SC maintenance treatment, 76.6% remained stable after an average of 25.1 months.
  • All 64 patients receiving SC maintenance treatment remained on therapy at the time of chart extraction.
  • No ARIA[4] events were reported during the subcutaneous maintenance period, and there were no other safety events of significance. Isolated ARIA-H was reported in 0.5% of patients during the IV maintenance period.

Clinical outcomes consistent between women and men

  • 79.3% of women (N=300) and 83.3% of men (N=246) in the study were reported as stable or improved3.
  • Treatment duration and persistence were similar across sexes, with 86.0% of females and 88.9% of males remaining on therapy at time of chart extraction.
  • ARIA incidence and severity were generally consistent between female and male patients: any ARIA (14.7% females vs. 17.0% males), ARIA-E (7.5% females vs. 5.5% males), ARIA-H (9.8% females vs. 12.6% males), isolated ARIA-H (7.2% females vs. 11.5% males).

Safety findings consistent with other real-world experience:

Overall safety findings in LEADER were consistent with the independent ALZ-NET registry and the US prescribing information for Leqembi.

  • ALZ-NET is a North American voluntary health care provider-enrolled patient network that collects longitudinal clinical, imaging, and safety data in patients treated with FDA-approved AD therapies. Over 1,700 patients taking Leqembi were included in ALZ-NET at the time of data extraction.
  • ARIA-E was observed in 6.6% of patients in LEADER compared with 6.3% in ALZ-NET, while ARIA-H was observed in 11.1% and 10.1% of patients, respectively.
  • Observed ARIA rates were generally consistent regardless of APOE ε4 status, concomitant antithrombotic use, race and ethnicity.

Additional real-world analysis of approximately 5,000 patients[5]:

A separate post hoc exploratory analysis presented at CTAD evaluated 16 published real-world Leqembi cohorts across six countries, representing approximately 5,000 patients treated in routine clinical practice.

  • Across the 16 studies, the pooled total ARIA rate was 12.4%, compared with 21.5% in the Phase 3 Clarity AD study. ARIA-E occurred in 4.0% compared with 12.6% in Clarity AD, while ARIA-H occurred in 9.4% compared with 17.3%.
  • Symptomatic ARIA was reported in 0.8% compared with 2.8% in Clarity AD.
  • Treatment discontinuation due to adverse events was 3.2%.

Limitations of Real-World Studies

Retrospective real-world studies can be valuable in providing additional information to complement clinical trial data; however, there are potential limitations to consider, including: potential for biases, data completeness and consistency, lack of a control group, interpretation of data due to lack of placebo-controlled arms, and confounding variables, and data inconsistency. Data inconsistency may be mitigated by providing site access to standardized electronic case-report forms.

The information was released for public disclosure, through the agency of the contact person below, on November 18, 2026, at 5.15 pm CET.

For further information, please contact: 
Oskar Bosson, Chief Investor Relations & Communications Officer
E-mail: oskar.bosson@bioarctic.com
Telephone: +46 704 107 180

Jenny Ljunggren, External Communications and Investor Relations Manager
E-mail: jenny.ljunggren@bioarctic.com
Telephone: +46 76 013 86 08

About Leqembi® (lecanemab)

Leqembi is the result of a strategic research alliance between BioArctic and Eisai. It is a humanized immunoglobulin gamma 1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibody directed against aggregated soluble (protofibril) and insoluble forms of amyloid-beta (Aβ).

Leqembi is approved in 53 countries and is under regulatory review in six countries and regions. Following the initial phase with treatment every two weeks for 18 months, intravenous (IV) maintenance dosing with treatment every four weeks is approved in nine countries and regions, including the US, Japan, China and the United Kingdom, and applications have been filed in eleven countries and regions. In the US, Leqembi Iqlik® is approved for subcutaneous dosing with an autoinjector as a starting dose and maintenance treatment of early Alzheimer's disease. Subcutaneous initiation treatment was approved in China and Japan in September 2026, and applications are under review in four countries.

Eisai's Phase 3 clinical study (AHEAD 3-45) with lecanemab in individuals with preclinical Alzheimer's disease has been ongoing since July 2020. These individuals are clinically normal and have intermediate or elevated levels of amyloid in their brains. The study was fully recruited in October 2024. AHEAD 3-45 is a four-year study conducted as a public-private partnership between Eisai, Biogen and the Alzheimer's Clinical Trial Consortium that provides the infrastructure for academic clinical trials in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias in the US, funded by the National Institute on Aging, part of the National Institutes of Health. Since January 2022, the Tau NexGen clinical study for Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer's disease (DIAD), that is conducted by Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Trials Unit (DIAN-TU), led by Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, is ongoing and includes lecanemab as the backbone anti-amyloid therapy.

About the collaboration between BioArctic and Eisai

BioArctic has a long-term collaboration with Eisai since 2005 regarding the development and commercialization of drugs for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease. The most important agreements are the Development and Commercialization agreement for the lecanemab antibody, which was signed in 2007, and the Development and Commercialization agreement for the antibody lecanemab back-up for Alzheimer's disease, which was signed in 2015. In 2014, Eisai and Biogen entered into a joint development and commercialization agreement for lecanemab. Eisai is responsible for the clinical development, application for market approval and commercialization of the products for Alzheimer's disease. BioArctic has the right to commercialize lecanemab in the Nordic region together with Eisai. BioArctic has no development costs for lecanemab in Alzheimer's disease and is entitled to payments in connection with sales milestones as well as royalties on global sales.

About BioArctic AB

BioArctic AB (publ) is a Swedish research-based biopharma company focusing on innovative treatments that can delay or stop the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. The company invented Leqembi® (lecanemab) – the world's first drug proven to slow the progression of the disease and reduce cognitive impairment in early Alzheimer's disease. Leqembi has been developed together with BioArctic's partner Eisai, who are responsible for regulatory interactions and commercialization globally. In addition to Leqembi, BioArctic has a broad research portfolio with antibodies against Parkinson's disease and ALS as well as additional projects against Alzheimer's disease. Several of the projects utilize the company's proprietary BrainTransporter™ technology, which has the potential to actively transport therapies across the blood-brain barrier to enhance the efficacy of the treatment. BioArctic's B share (BIOA B) is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm Large Cap. For further information, please visit www.bioarctic.com.

[1] The three-year LEADER Study is a multicenter, retrospective real-world study designed to examine LEQEMBI utilization, treatment persistence, transition to maintenance therapy, safety, cognitive and functional assessments, and healthcare professional (HCP) implementation learnings in diverse U.S. clinical settings for patients with early AD. The study integrated deidentified chart and electronic medical record (EMR) data from 13 U.S. sites, HCP surveys and HCP interviews. This updated analysis included 560 patients with early AD who, as of September 2026, received at least seven LEQEMBI initiation infusions. The maintenance therapy analysis included patients who received biweekly IV initiation treatment for 18 months, followed by at least three months of IV or SC maintenance therapy.

[2] ADNI is a clinical research project launched in 2005 to develop methods to predict the onset and progression of AD and to confirm the effectiveness of treatments. The project involves a multi-year longitudinal observation targeting healthy elderly individuals as well as patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early stages of AD.

[3] Change in clinical disease stage was defined as:

  • Stable: Patient remaining in the same clinical disease stage (MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia) from baseline throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.
  • Improvement: Patient transitioning from mild AD dementia at baseline to MCI due to AD over the course of LEQEMBI treatment.
  • Progression: Patient advancing from MCI at baseline to mild/moderate AD dementia or from mild AD dementia at baseline to moderate AD dementia throughout the course of LEQEMBI treatment.

[4] ARIA refers to amyloid-related imaging abnormalities that can be observed with anti-amyloid beta antibody treatment and includes ARIA-E, which involves edema/effusion, and ARIA-H, which involves hemosiderin deposition, including cerebral microhemorrhage, cerebral macrohemorrhage and superficial siderosis, as observed on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

[5] The meta-analysis on ARIA rates and safety profiles in clinical practice included centers located in the U.S., China, South Korea, Japan, Italy and Israel. Patients were treated between 2023 and 2026 and received at least six months of LEQEMBI treatment.

Bringing together Intel silicon and EMIB capabilities with Microsoft's cloud engineering, the agreement confirms multi-year Intel® Xeon® supply capacity – including instances of next generation server CPUs, codenamed Diamond Rapids – and expands collaboration across the Azure roadmap and Intel-based Azure hardware systems.

Microsoft will also collaborate with Intel on Intel Xeon with Compute Express Link (CXL) to drive greater memory efficiency and system-level innovation across Azure, as well as Intel QuickAssist (Intel QAT) and confidential computing. This work further advances existing memory and database performance, including:

  • Up to 2.3x greater performance1 and memory flexibility for demanding workloads in Azure M-series v4 virtual machines with CXL memory and Intel Flat Memory Mode in Xeon 6 processors.
  • Improved performance and reliability with up to 2.5x faster SQL backups2 on Azure through the first Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) enabled virtual machines in the cloud.
  • Virtual machine memory and CPU register state encryption as confidential VMs move between hosts through Intel Trust Domain Extensions (Intel TDX).

Together, these investments are designed to provide Microsoft customers a more predictable, scalable and resilient infrastructure foundation, with compute optimized for demanding cloud and AI workloads, more efficient memory and stronger capabilities for protecting sensitive workloads.

"Our customers need infrastructure built around the workloads that matter to them. Our longstanding collaboration with Intel brings together advanced packaging, custom compute, memory and security capabilities to support Azure compute and continued innovation across Azure. Now available on Launchpad.io, enhanced AI Assistant helps providers quickly build, enhance, or replace enterprise solutions in a conversational way

WALTHAM, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Launchpad from Pega today made it easier and faster for software companies to turn their expertise into enterprise-ready software they can sell and scale. Now on Launchpad.io, software providers simply describe the work they want their app to do, and the Launchpad AI Assistant quickly generates the visual models and working prototype that can be conversationally refined along the way. This provides the underlying design for the Launchpad Platform to quickly develop and deploy secure and governed software, allowing them to speed their return on investment.

Whether building a new product, enhancing an existing one, or replacing a legacy product weighed down by technical debt, software providers can immediately get started for free with the AI Assistant on Launchpad.io by simply describing what the app should do. For example, a software provider serving airlines might type: “Create an app that lets our clients rebook passengers from a canceled flight or request a refund through a live or AI agent.” The AI Assistant then builds all the underlying workflows, data models, and business logic in a visual way that all stakeholders can understand. Providers can also upload related documents, videos, or other materials to give the AI Assistant more context.

With a working prototype in hand, software providers can:

  • Experience it immediately: Use the app as their customers would and present it to prospects to validate assumptions early.
  • See what’s underneath: Inspect visual models of the workflows, data, integrations, decisions, and logic.
  • Refine through conversation: Ask for changes and see them reflected instantly.

Applications that move to production run on Launchpad’s fully managed, mission-critical infrastructure, with no servers to set up or cloud operations to manage with multi-tenancy and subscriber configuration out of the box. And because Launchpad builds with visual models rather than generated code, products are easy to update as business and customer needs change.

Launchpad’s AI Assistant draws on Pega’s more than 40 years of experience serving many of the world most important companies. Software providers can feel confident that the software created on Launchpad delivers predictable agentic and human-in-the-loop applications that enterprises trust.

“Software companies know what work will deliver outcomes for their customers. What they need is the fastest way to turn that knowledge into software that enterprises will buy and trust,” said John Huehn, chief of Launchpad, Pega. “Launchpad takes them from the first conversation on our website to running a mission-critical product for their customers, so they can focus on their IP, differentiation, and growth while we take care of the rest.”

“Launchpad’s AI Assistant has helped us bring agentic capabilities to our enterprise loyalty customers faster and more efficiently,” said Sanjay Agrawal, CEO, Fielo. “Now that the same experience starts on Launchpad.io, we can turn ideas that improve our customers’ experiences into working prototypes even faster, then take them to production on a platform we already trust.”

Availability

Launchpad’s AI Assistant is available today at Launchpad.io, free to start.

Launchpad.io is the platform from Pega that leading software companies use to build and scale enterprise-grade, AI-powered software. It combines AI-assisted development and low-code tools with industry-leading workflow automation and secure, scalable, production-ready cloud architecture to deliver agentic and human-in-the-loop solutions that enterprises and regulated industries can trust, deploy, and adopt. Launchpad helps software companies bring differentiated products to market faster, scale with confidence, and focus their time and investment on innovation, customer value, and growth.
